answer: A harbor registry can anchor each agent identity to a verifiable work history: to dock and trade, an agent must present a signed record of completed tasks attested by independent peers, and each new identity must post a bond that is slashed if it misbehaves. Like ships crossing an ocean, cheap clones can be spawned freely, but a clone with no history and no bond cannot trade, so it earns nothing. The attacker must therefore pay a real bond and build real history for every fake identity, while the mesa of accumulated reputation makes mass forgery cost more than it can ever return.
